functions.doc: 1 while playing; 0 once a tune that does not loop is over

functions.name: tune_samples
functions.doc: Digi voices (tune45's d1: .. d4:): samples on the audio DMA. A hit sets its channel up and starts it (8-bit unsigned, once, at the volume on both sides); the next hit on the channel cuts it short (tune45 mixes samples hit together into one, and warns of tails cut short). The audio DMA reads chip RAM only: tune_samples where the tunes' samples are (tune45's tune_sample_bank, or its --samples file loaded): chip RAM, not across a 64 KB boundary tune_digi_channels the audio DMA channel (0-3) of digi voice 0 (before tune_play; voices past channel 3 are left out): the others stay the program's, for its sound effects tune_digi_volume 0-255 (255 at first) They stay set across tune_play.

functions.name: tune_seek
functions.doc: On ticks ticks at once, silently (after tune_play: back where a tune was, from tune_ticks; tune45 gives a tune's TUNE_<NAME>_TICKS, once through, to keep a looping tune's position short). The voices sound again from their next events. Interrupts are held off while it runs (about 0.2 ms a thousand ticks of a voice).

functions.name: tune_update
functions.doc: Once a frame (50 Hz PAL, 60 Hz NTSC: the tempo is the same in time)

functions.name: tune_voices
functions.doc: Run-time controls (they stay set across tune_play): tune_voices the SID voice of tune voice 0 (before tune_play) tune_tempo a tempo scale, 8.8: 0x100 as written, 0x140 1.25 times as fast tune_vibrato vibrato depth added to every note's (a wobble) tune_transpose / tune_detune per tune voice: semitones; frequency + amount/64 of itself (a chorus, out of tune)

functions.name: tune_volume
functions.doc: For a game: the music's volume, voices lent to the program's sound effects, the next tune at a bar line. tune_volume the music's volume 0-15 (15 at first): the SIDs' (their $D418 volume, the rest of it kept) and the digi voices' (17 a step, times tune_digi_volume's); at once tune_fade to a volume over so many frames (tune_update steps it); tune_fading: 1 until it gets there. A fade out and the next tune: tune_fade(50, 0) ... tune_play ... tune_fade(50, 15) tune_borrow a tune voice (0-11) lent to the program for so many frames (0: until tune_return): the music goes on but writes none of its registers (nor its filter routing), so a sound effect can play on it (audio_sid.h); back, it sounds again from its next note tune_queue the tune started at the playing one's next bar line (its ticks a multiple of bar: tune45 gives TUNE_<NAME>_BAR for a tune with ticks a bar), or at once if on one or nothing plays; tune_queued: 1 while it waits The volume stays set across tune_play.
